recipes.name: Fluffy Strawberry Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Mix strawberry-flavored gelatin mix, sugar, and boiling water together in a large bowl, stirring until gelatin and sugar have dissolved.
Refrigerate gelatin mixture until it begins to turn thick and syrupy, about 10 minutes.
Gently fold frozen whipped topping into gelatin mixture until thoroughly combined.
Fold the 2 1/2 cups of sliced strawberries into whipped topping mixture.
Spoon filling into graham cracker crust and decorate edge of filling with 8 strawberry halves.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Fluffy Strawberry Pie
raw_recipe.description: This strawberry fluffy pie is made with sweet filling, plenty of fresh strawberries, and whipped topping, then loaded into a graham cracker crust.

video.description: Nothing is better than fresh, fruity, and sweet strawberry pie! It’s so creamy, fluffy, and full of strawberries!

review.reviewBody: Being a diabetic I made a couple of changes to this recipe substituting sugar with Splenda, regular jello to sugar-free and used sugar-free Cool Whip. This is a refreshing delightful pie. My family loved it. Thank you for sharing it!

Loved the taste and it was easy to make. Everyone in book club loved it! I used regular Jello and Tru Whip topping as these had the least artificial ingredients. After 10 min in fridge, it wasn’t “thick and soupy” so I kept adding additional minutes; too long, as the Jello in the bottom of the bowl started to thicken. Picked out the long thick pieces and incorporated the smaller bits, giving the dessert bits of red speckle. However, I agree with others that this turns into more of a mousse, even after being in fridge for 6 hours and freezer for 1 hour. I can see this as a parfait with crumbled graham crackers.
Going to try it with fresh whipped cream instead of using the whipped cream from store.

Made as written and really good but a little sweet. I made my own graham cracker crust. I think you can omit or scale down the added sugar. I also think this can be made with real, sweetened whipped cream and sugar free jell-o if you want to make it healthier. I also think you can use different fruit- raspberries w/ raspberry jell-o, peaches with peach jell-o, etc. But as is, very good!

I made this for a friend who just had a baby girl (fun pink dessert!) and made one for our family. It was light and delicious. I made it a little healthier with low-fat cool whip and truvia instead of the sugar. I would have used sugar-free Jello but the store was out. I may try it with fresh peaches and peach Jello next time.

It was easy to make. I would make sure the strawberries that you add to the whipped cream are blotted dry before mixing them in. It can make the mixture a little runny. Another tip is to eat it within the first 2-3 days. It was very tasty and my friends really enjoyed it.

Doubled and put in 9x13 pan. Used single package of strawberries and no graham crackers. Added cool whip about 35 minutes after refrigeration. Very good. 3 adults and 2 children gobbled this down in one night.
It was light n fluffy but I made it my own! I added a can of pineapple tidbits n also replaced the water with the pineapple juice! I also didn’t make as a pie!! I put it in parfait glasses!
This was very good. I made into parfait cups since didn't want to have crust. Just served with a strawberry partially sliced and fanned out on each cup. Nice!!

I recall seeing this recipe in a magazine ad for Jello in a Woman’s Day or Family Circle! It may also be made with peaches and peach jello (do they still make that?). Drain the (frozen or canned) peaches well. Love the sugar free version listed in comments.
I will definitely make it again in the strawberry version. But today I have substitute out the strawberries for cherries.
The only issue I had was it was runny. I'm experimenting with additional time for the jello to stay in the fridge
I hate to waste food.
My Grandma made a pie just like this my entire life as I grew up, except she used Dream Whip instead of Whipped Cream. I followed this recipe and it tasted just like my Grandma's did.
I served this pie after a family BBQ. It was the perfect finish to an evening meal The weather was scorching, but this light and fluffy dessert was welcomed by all.

Great flavor and refreshing summer treat. The family loved it. I think ill put strawberries on top or just less in the mix because it did get runny. Ill definitely make this again. Oh and i did put more whip cream than stated cause you need a good thick consistency and not let the jello mix take over cause then it will be runny from the start.

The first time I made this my extended family loved it and now ask me to bring it to family functions. I usually double the recipe and put it in a 9 x 13 pan. It's delicious and a lighter dessert alternative than my usual chocolate and peanut butter combo. My Aunt Judy asked for the recipe because "This has given (uncle) Rob my pleasure than I ever have." It's that good.
Made this for company today. When I cut into the pie it was like soup. I had it in the refrigerator for about 3 hours. It was a mess.
Delicious
I will be making this...Maybe softened cream cheese folded in?
